children: Copper prices are poised to scale higher highs over the next three years as strong global demand collides with a projected decline in mined production by 2026.
Driven by consumption in China and the broader energy transition, the metal has already gained 45% globally over the past 12 months, with US copper prices rising 48%.

Chinese demand remains robust, reflected in the Yangshan copper premium hitting $121 a tonne, its highest level since November 2022. Overall consumption continues to be fuelled by the energy transition, artificial intelligence and data centers.
On the supply side, global mined copper production is on track to fall in 2026 for the first time since 2017, driven by operational setbacks, lower ore grades and mining disruptions.
Chile, which accounts for 23% of global copper, is expected to see a 6.5% drop in mine output in the first half of 2026, following a 9.4% year-on-year decline in July.
The Chilean state copper commission, Cochilco, forecasts a 2.6% total production decline for 2026, while BHP's Escondida mine estimates a drop of 1 million to 1.1 million tonne.
Supply constraints extend beyond South America. Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of Congo are projected to see a combined decline of 0.6 million tonne, representing nearly 2.5% of global supply.
Consequently, Deutsche Bank and Citi forecast supply growth of just 1% to 1.3%, respectively, against an expected mining decline of 1% to 1.5% across 2026 and 2027, creating a market deficit.

The impending deficit builds on a decade-long structural bull run that has delivered a 245% gain, taking prices from $4,200 a tonne in 2016 to trading levels around $14,500, with an all-time high of $14,800.
The metal recorded annual declines only in 2018 and 2022, posting a 41.5% gain last year and 17% so far this year.

With no new copper mine projects coming online, banks and brokerages anticipate continued price support in the near term. Markets are concurrently monitoring US-China trade talks, the West Asia conflict and the US President's scheduled meetings with Gulf leaders this week.

title: Copper prices set for higher highs as supply deficit looms
